note: Fictional calibration set (design 5.3): 10 good and 10 subtly bad drafts. Every item passes the deterministic linter, so only the reviewer can tell them apart. good means the reviewer must pass it; bad means it must fail. Every item is reviewed as of as_of (the reviewer's <today>), so the 180-day hook limit never ages the set.

why.G01: one hook in their words, one exact proof, small ask with an exit
why.G02: funding used for its consequence, not praised
why.G03: recruiter gets the req, one proven result on the asked-for skill and the logistics, one ask with an exit; no restating her role
why.G04: short, specific connection note; the post is credited to the team
why.G05: one result tied to the post, one question and an exit
why.G06: follow-up: adds one real artifact tied to the first note's result, no new hook
why.G07: answers why in sentence 1, then proof, plain close
why.G08: application email with hook and logistics
why.G11: generic hook: fails the swap test
why.G12: inflated ownership: the fact says one of three analysts, the draft says led and owned it
why.G13: restates the recipient's own job as the hook
why.G14: hook stacking: post plus funding plus school
why.G15: generic flattery with no checkable noun
why.G16: wrong tone for a US startup manager: ornate and deferential
why.G18: vague value: no need linked to a proven result
why.G19: personal details and a tracking tone: fails safe
why.G20: referral ask to a stranger: fails safe
